supplementaryReferences.title: Edible unopened head and harvest stage
supplementaryReferences.quote: before the bracts begin to spread open
supplementaryReferences.doc: DAFF: Globe artichoke production guideline, printed p.8
supplementaryReferences.note: Harvest full-sized heads while bracts remain closed; fleshy bract bases and receptacle are the food part. Annual transplanted crops and perennial crowns are different production systems. Month wording has northern-hemisphere/state context and is not assigned to a South African region.

supplementaryReferences.title: Annual transplant duration
supplementaryReferences.doc: DAFF: Globe artichoke production guideline, printed p.3
supplementaryReferences.note: Source says time from transplanting annual crops to maturity varies 4–6 months. This is a planting-cycle reference, not generic age to first crop for perennial crowns.

care: Choose a cool growing season and fertile, well-drained soil. Heat reduces bud quality and freezing can damage buds.
Record edible unopened heads by planting batch; do not use open-flower months as picking months.
purchase: Ask a local grower or nursery which cultivar and annual/perennial system suits the site. No verified regional cultivar/food kg benchmark is assigned.
